text: Sada Social Reports 951 Digital Violations Targeting Palestinian Content in October Sada Social Center for Digital Rights has documented 951 digital violations targeting Palestinian content and its supporters across various online platforms during October. According to the report, 915 violations targeted individual users, while 30 cases involved direct actions by digital plattorms themselves. Most incidents were recorded on X (450), Telegram (317), and Facebook (148), including campaigns of account deletion, restriction, and suspension affecting users who documented Israeli violations or expressed solidarity with victims. Escalation of Online Incitement Against Journalists and Activists Sada Social observed a sharp increase in digital incitement and hate campaigns targeting Palestinian journalists and content creators, among them: Noha Al-Shaghaf, Hani Abu Riza, Mahmoud Al-Amoudi, Safinaz Al-Louh, Tamer Al-Mishal, Asmaa Al-Madhoon, Saed Al-Za'anin, Saleh Al-Ja'afrawi, Muna Al-Kurd, Tamer Dabbouseh, Dr. Rami Abdu, and Jad Qadumi, who was later arrested following a wave of online incitement. Additional cases included incitement against journalist Jivara Al-Budeiri and lawyer Mohannad Karajah, as well as hate speech targeting freed prisoner Musab Qafisheh, who was subsequently re-arrested by Israeli forces. Institutional Incitement from Hebrew Media Sada Social documented organized digital incitement campaigns by Hebrew-language media outlets targeting entire Palestinian communities, followed by military raids by Israeli forces-reflecting the direct translation of digital hate into real-world violence. Following the recent prisoner exchange, the Center also recorded an alarming rise in hate speech against released detainees, including public calls for "execution" and "physical elimination," constituting direct incitement to violence.

text: "Rakevet" Prison... the Cell That Never Sees the Light Human rights reports reveal a secret Israeli underground prison known as Rakevet, where dozens of Palestinians from Gaza are held in total isolation from the world. Detainees are deprived of sunlight and sufficient food, confined in windowless cells amid accounts of beatings and abuse. text: U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen confirms that Israel has been detaining the American child Mohammad Ibrahim (16 years old) for nine months without trial. text: The scars of war don't sit on the body alone-they settle deep in the small eyes that learned loss far too early. Today at the Prosthetics Center, I found Ravan sitting in her wheelchair, staring at a row of artificial limbs lined across the chairs, as if she were looking at pieces of her stolen childhood. She whispered to me, "Every time I see a child playing... I feel like I'm losing my leg all over again." A little girl who was meant to run, not count her wounds; meant to laugh, not face the emptiness the war carved inside her. Ravan didn't just lose her leg—she lost her normal days, her play, her first steps, and now she's forced to gather herself with hands far smaller than the weight she carries. The International Day of Persons with Disabilities isn't an occasion—it's an alarm to the world that Gaza holds thousands of children trying to continue life with half a body and a full heartbeat. Ravan... a small witness to a war far bigger than all of us, her pain screaming even when she stays silent. ندوبُ الحرب لا تسكن الأجساد فقط، بل تستقرّ في العيون الصغيرة التي فهمت الفقد قبل ما تكبر. اليوم كنت في مركز الأطراف الصناعية، وهناك كانت رقان جالسة على كرسيّها تتأمل صفّ الأطراف المعلّقة أمامها، كأنها تتفرّج على طفولتها المعلّقة على كراسي فارغة. همستلي: "كل ما أشوف طفل بلعب... بحس رجلي بتنقص مني مرة ثانية " طفلة كان المفروض تركض مش تُحصي جراحها، تضحك مش تواجه هذا الفراغ اللي تركته الحرب جواها. رقان ما فقدتش رجلها بس! فقدت جزءًا من يومها العادي، من لعبتها، من خطواتها الأولى، وصارت مضطرة تجمع نفسها بيدين أصغر من الوجع. اليوم العالمي لذوي الإعاقة مش مناسبة، هو صفّارة وجع للعالم كله: إن في غزة آلاف الأطفال اللي بيحاولوا يكملوا حياتهم بنصف جسد وروح مطفية.

text: Did you know Palestinian women have always been a central force in the struggle against Israeli colonialism? Despite neoliberal feminist rhetoric and Zionist propaganda that seek to erase or distort their role, women have played a decisive part in anti-colonial resistance, especially during the First Intifada. The Palestinian women's struggle took shape under British colonial rule, alongside the rise of the Palestinian national liberation movement. This marked the first organized framework of women's opposition to British oppression that facilitated Zionist immigration and repressed Palestinian demands for self-determination. Across Palestine, women's committees played a crucial role during the Great Revolt of 1936-1939, when even peasant women were prepared to take up arms to detend their villages. When the First Intifada erupted in 1987, women swarmed the streets, threw stones at soldiers, transported supplies, built roadblocks, and confronted the occupation to counter crackdowns. These spontaneous actions soon developed into weekly, women-led protests. Palestinian women stood at the forefront of the popular committees that spread through towns and villages, sustaining the Intifada and organizing daily life during rebellion.

text: The death of Palestinian actor and director Mohammad Bakri, at the age of 72, following a rich artistic career filled with achievements. Artist Bakri passed away at Nahariya Hospital after suffering from heart disease, according to his family. Bakri is considered one of the most prominent figures in Palestinian cinema and theater, leaving a lasting mark on both the Arab and international scenes through dozens of works in acting, directing, and production. Israeli occupation authorities persecuted Bakri for many years, forcing him to face numerous court trials related to his artistic work and cultural productions, especially after directing his documentary film “Jenin, Jenin.” His theatrical career began with the play “A View from the Bridge” by playwright Arthur Miller, after which he continued participating in local theater productions, alongside notable film works such as “Behind Bars,” “Haifa,” “Private,” and “Under the Feet of Women.” وفاة الممثّل والمخرج الفلسطيني محمد بكري، عن عمر يناهز 72 عامًا، بعد مسيرة فنيّة حافلة بالإنجازات الفنيّة. توفي الفنان بكري، في مستشفى نهريا، بعد معاناة مع أمراض القلب، وفق ما أفادت أسرته. يُعد بكري أحد أبرز الأسماء في السينما والمسرح الفلسطيني، إذ ترك بصمة في المشهدين العربي والدولي، عبر عشرات الأعمال التي شارك فيها تمثيلًا وإخراجًا وإنتاجًا. سلطات الاحـ ـتلال لاحقت الفنان بكري، لسنوات طويلة، أُجبر خلالها على خوض محاكمات عديدة تتعلّق بعمله الفنّي وإنتاجاته الثقافية، وبخاصّة بعد إخراج فيلمه الوثائقي"جنين جنين". انطلقت مسيرته المسرحية بعرض "مشهد من الجسر" للكاتب آرثر ميلر، ثم واصل المشاركة في أعمال مسرحية محلية، إلى جانب أعمال سينمائية بارزة مثل "وراء القضبان"، و"حيفا"، و"برايفيت"، و"تحت أقدام النساء".
